stem:
Neil must rewrite $4 \times (7 + 5)$ as a sum of products that keeps the same value.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call the answer a multiple of a sum, and stop there.
Write $4 \times 7 + 5$, so only $7$ is multiplied by $4$.
Write $4 \times 7 + 4 \times 5$, multiplying each part of the sum by $4$.
Say the expanded sum $4 \times 7 + 4 \times 5$ is what creates the factored form $4 \times (7 + 5)$.

teacher.key_rationale: The distributive property expands 4×(7+5) as 4×7+4×5. Naming only "multiple of a sum" substitutes a label. Leaving 5 unmultiplied confuses the operation on each part. Saying the expansion creates the factored form reverses the relation.
